packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, isolated image-only reader (Claude Code subagent)
text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement
No proposed identification of work or author, and no earlier reading, reached me in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..008.jpg (plus the filtered filename listing described in packet-01.txt). The images themselves show a modern ownership stamp and a pencil shelf-number (transcribed below as modern additions); I have drawn no conclusion from them.

Layout survey (observation)
- Two faces of one narrow vertical parchment strip. image-001 = overview of face A; image-002, -003, -004 = its native tiles top to bottom, overlapping. image-005 = overview of face B; image-006, -007, -008 = its tiles, overlapping.
- The strip is only about 3 to 6 letters wide, cut vertically out of a leaf, so every line is a short middle slice: both ends of every line are lost. It is folded lengthwise down the middle and pierced by a row of lozenge-shaped holes on the fold (sewing stations: tentative interpretation, a sewing guard).
- Script: a large, round, upright minuscule in orange-brown ink, generously spaced; tall s, uncial-looking d beside straight d, ct/st ligatures. Horizontal drypoint ruling is visible on both faces. One line of writing per ruled line.
- Face A: 16 written lines, then blank parchment; below the blank, two or three faint orange-red capital letters (looks like rubric or display capitals, much paler than the text). Face B: 20 written lines, then blank.
- No running title, no enlarged initial, no underlining, no interlinear or marginal gloss is visible; but the crop is far too narrow to show margins or column structure. Whether the leaf had one column or two cannot be told. Which face is recto is unknown; "A" and "B" are only my labels.
- Medial points (punctus) occur on face A lines 3 and 12 and probably 15.
- Modern additions: a round black ink stamp on each face (face A legible in part: "ÖSTERR. NATION[...]" around the top, lower arc "[...]BLIOTHEK"? reversed/partly inked; face B the same stamp, faint) and on face A, in pencil written sideways, "Fragm. 36" (last digit 6 or 8). Face B has a pencil mark like "3" above the stamp.

Areas selected / unread
- Everything written on both faces is transcribed; nothing was skipped. Since no line gives more than one word plus a fragment, there is no connected prose to choose between.

TRANSCRIPTION - FACE A
Convention: ] and [ mark the cut edges; every line is broken at both ends. A macron is shown as a combining stroke where I see one. Tall s is given as s.

Tile image-002 (lines counted from top of that image)
image-002 l.1   ]ibus[            (first letter trimmed; "bus" clear)
image-002 l.2   ]s a͞nc?[          (tall letter, then "anc" or "ant" with a horizontal stroke over the n and following letter; could be "ante" or "anc"; last letter cut)
image-002 l.3   ]a · un?[         (punctus after "a"; then "u" + minims, "un" or "ui" + one more minim)
image-002 l.4   ]terpr?[          ("terp" clear; final letter r or i; a descending flourish under the r/p; a minim before t is possible, so "]iterpr" / "(in)terpr"?)
image-002 l.5   ]s secur[         (a tall stroke before "secur", probably s or f of the previous word)
image-002 l.6   ]l? tui?[         (first letter a tall stroke, l or the shaft of another letter; then "tui" or "tin")
image-002 l.7   ]de ad[           (written close: "dead"; I take it as "de ad" but "dead" as one string is what is on the leaf)
image-002 l.8   ]rn̄e la[          (macron over "ne"; then "la" with the a trimmed, or "li")
image-002 l.9   ]nimar?[          (bottom of tile, letters cut below; see image-003 l.2)

Tile image-003
image-003 l.1   = image-002 l.8 (overlap): ]rn̄e la[
image-003 l.2   = image-002 l.9 (overlap): ]nimar[ or ]n mar[   (minims: "nmar"; last letter r or the start of another letter)
image-003 l.3   ]t? uita[         (cut letter with a cross-stroke, t or c; "uita" or "uite", final letter trimmed)
image-003 l.4   ]dn̄e d[           (stroke over "ne": d(omi)ne; then round d and a trimmed letter)
image-003 l.5   ]ueni? · [        ("uem" or "ueni", minims ambiguous; punctus; then the left curve of a round letter)
image-003 l.6   ]bsolu[           (first letter trimmed: round bowl, b or o; so "]bsolu[" , (a)bsolu?)
image-003 l.7   ]nos co[          (possibly "]inos"; "co" followed by a trimmed letter)
image-003 l.8   ]ritui? · [       (a tall trimmed letter, then "itui" or "rtui"/"ritui"; a point or the start of a letter after)
image-003 l.9   ]t? cus[          (a trimmed final stroke of a word, then "cus" and the start of a further letter, perhaps t)

Tile image-004
image-004 l.1   = image-003 l.9 (overlap), only the tops "cu" visible.
image-004       [modern stamp]
image-004 l.2   ]?H[ or ]IH[      (faint orange-red capitals, much faded: an upright, then a clear H, then a trace; possibly "UH" or "IH" or "TH"; I cannot decide. Tentatively a rubric or display line.)
image-004       [pencil, sideways] Fragm. 36 (last digit 6 or 8)

TRANSCRIPTION - FACE B

Tile image-006
image-006 l.1   ]am t[            (possibly "]iam" / "]lam": a trimmed stroke before a)
image-006 l.2   ]ation[           (or "]atior"; first letter trimmed; last letter n or r)
image-006 l.3   ]is ho[
image-006 l.4   ]ntiar?[          ("ntia" clear; last letter r or first stroke of m)
image-006 l.5   ]pecca[
image-006 l.6   ]mur[             (possibly "]imur"; a minim trimmed at left)
image-006 l.7   ]salua[           (last letter trimmed, a or the start of another)
image-006 l.8   ]am t[
image-006 l.9   ]misist[          (bottom of tile; see image-007 l.3)

Tile image-007
image-007 l.1   = image-006 l.7 (overlap), bottoms only.
image-007 l.2   = image-006 l.8 (overlap): ]am t[
image-007 l.3   ]misist[          (or "]nisist"; st ligature at the edge)
image-007 l.4   ]enter-?[         ("enter" with a horizontal stroke running off from the r to the edge: either a ligature into a following letter or an abbreviation stroke)
image-007 l.5   ]' dn̄e[           (a small raised mark or the tail of a letter, then d(omi)ne with stroke; blank after, to the edge)
image-007 l.6   ]filius [         (a short stroke after s at the edge, a point or a hyphen-like mark)
image-007 l.7   ]b; ? inu[        (first sign looks like a b with a suspension hook, i.e. -b(us), or possibly a q(ue) sign; then "inu")
image-007 l.8   ]t? exp[          (trimmed letter with cross-stroke; "exp" then the start of a round letter)
image-007 l.9   ]luer?[           ("lu" clear, preceded by a trimmed stroke, so perhaps "]dluer"/"]iluer"; then a round letter, e or o, + r with a stroke to the edge; "luor"/"luer")
image-007 l.10  ]rtib; p?[        ("tib" with an -us hook: -tib(us); a trimmed r or t before; then, set lower and at the edge, a tall letter, p or s)
image-007 l.11  ]ut m[            (the m trimmed, could be n)

Tile image-008
image-008 l.1   = image-007 l.10 (overlap)
image-008 l.2   = image-007 l.11 (overlap): ]ut m[
image-008 l.3   ]mnia[            (minims: "nnia" / "mnia"; (o)mnia?)
image-008 l.4   ]riter?[          (or "]nter" / "]rıtcr"; the letter after t is e or c; last letter r trimmed)
image-008 l.5   ]discip[          (last letter p trimmed, only the shaft)
image-008       [blank, then modern stamp, faint; pencil "3"?]

Observations kept apart from interpretation
- Observed words or word-parts I am confident of: ibus, secur, de ad, dn̄e (twice, one on each face), bsolu, nos co, cus; am t (twice), is ho, pecca, mur, salua, misist, filius, exp, tib(us), ut, discip.
- Tentative: the repeated vocative-looking dn̄e, with pecca-, salua-, -bsolu-, misist-, suggests a text of address or prayer rather than exposition. That is an inference from vocabulary only and I have not tried to place it.
- No abbreviation was expanded silently; the only expansions offered are d(omi)ne and -b(us), in parentheses.

Limitations
- Each line preserves roughly 4 to 7 letters out of a line of unknown length. No line can be joined to the next. A source match would have to rely on the vertical sequence of fragments at a fixed column position, not on any continuous phrase.
- Minim groups (un/ui, uem/ueni, nmar/nimar, mnia/nnia, tui/tin) are genuinely ambiguous and I have left them so.
- The central fold swallows part of one letter in several lines (face A l.2, l.4, l.6; face B l.4, l.9), so a narrow letter may be hidden there.
- The faded capitals at the foot of face A deserve a contrast-enhanced or UV image.
- A wider view is impossible from this strip; sister strips from the same binding, if any exist, would be the useful next thing to image.
